author: Declaration Desk
title: Zelensky warns of new Russian mass strike on Ukraine's grid as talks stall over land
dek: Ukraine says intelligence points to an imminent attack on energy and logistics after 113 drones and ballistic missiles hit six regions. US envoy Jared Kushner says negotiations are in 'a little bit of a deadlock'.
body:
President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Thursday that Ukrainian intelligence indicates Russia is "completing preparations for a new massive strike" on Ukraine's energy system, logistics and essential services, and urged people to watch air-raid alerts closely in the coming days. "Unfortunately, we have information that the Russians are preparing another massive strike," he said in his evening address, adding: "We will respond to every Russian strike."

The warning came after Russia launched ballistic missiles and 113 drones overnight into Thursday, cutting power in six regions, Mr Zelensky said. On the diplomatic track, US envoy Jared Kushner said talks he is mediating with Steve Witkoff have hit "a little bit of a deadlock" over the fate of Ukrainian territory, according to reports. Neither side's battlefield claims could be independently verified.

## What happened

Ukraine's air force reported impacts at 20 locations from the overnight attack, and officials said an apartment building, a hospital, a sports facility, businesses and a petrol station were damaged, according to reports. "The Russians continue to target substations, overhead power lines, and the entire power grid," Mr Zelensky said. He listed Dnipro, Pavlohrad and other communities in the Dnipropetrovsk region, along with Kharkiv, Odesa, Sumy, Donetsk and Mykolaiv, as areas where conditions were worsening. On 25 November a Russian ballistic missile hit a shopping centre and other civilian buildings in Kyiv, according to reports.

Kyiv is pressing its partners for more air defence, especially Patriot interceptors, which can stop ballistic missiles but have been in short supply. Earlier this week Mr Zelensky said US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth had not yet approved the delivery of 48 Patriot interceptors that Ukraine's allies had already paid for, according to reports. The Pentagon has not explained the delay.

Ukraine kept up its own long-range strikes. Its General Staff said it hit a Russian military airfield and an oil pumping facility in two overnight attacks. Russia's defence ministry said its forces intercepted 343 Ukrainian drones overnight over 15 Russian regions, Crimea and the Azov and Black seas. Moscow-installed officials said a Ukrainian drone strike on a car park in occupied Zaporizhzhia killed five people, and local officials in Russia's Krasnodar region said four people were wounded, according to reports.

## The talks

Mr Kushner said on a podcast that Vladimir Putin wants peace, but added: "what (Putin) is saying is peace, but I think it's always peace on what terms." He also said Mr Putin "has agreed not to use nuclear weapons", calling it "a big thing", according to reports. Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov said in remarks posted on his ministry's website that Washington understood the need to address what Moscow calls the "root causes" of the conflict and was "open to dialogue".

President Donald Trump, who met Mr Putin in China earlier this month, said on social media that he wanted the Russian leader to "pull back all Military aggression against territories throughout Europe", and urged both armies to avoid actions that could "expand the War", according to reports. Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said the war "should not and cannot be expanded to the Mediterranean", after Ukraine said it struck a Russian naval vessel at a Libyan port with sea drones last weekend.

Mr Kushner did not set out what either side has offered on territory, which he described as the main sticking point.

## Why it matters for India

India has called throughout the war for dialogue and diplomacy. A new phase of strikes on energy targets on both sides, including Ukraine's attacks on Russian refineries and pipelines, feeds into oil prices that matter to India, which imports most of its crude. Any widening of the war into the Mediterranean would also touch shipping routes used by Indian trade with Europe.

## What happens next

The US administration is trying to arrange another round of talks before Christmas. Ukraine is bracing for the strike its intelligence has warned of, with winter demand on its grid rising.
